changed_in.5.2: A `message` of `nil` now counts as no message at all and a traceback is built for it. Earlier versions treat `nil` like any other value no text can be made of and hand it straight back, so `debug.traceback(nil)` answers `nil` there and describes nothing. A `level` that is neither a number nor a string reading as one also raises from here, where earlier versions ignore it and start from the default.
changed_in.5.3: A `level` carrying a fraction is refused rather than being cut down to a whole number, and so is one too large to hold an exact whole-number value.
